candidates.title: [Bug]: cloneWithType/fromJsonWithType with a union of structural types picks a member that needs lossy conversion over an exact match
[Bug]: `readonly & T` has no filler value (list filling panics with "no filler value")
candidates.body:
### Description
Filling a list whose member type is `readonly & T` fails: at runtime `a[1] = [7]` on a `(readonly & int[])[]` panics with `no filler value`, and at compile time `[int, readonly & int[]] t = [1];` is rejected with `type 'readonly&[int...]' has no filler value`. The same happens for `(readonly & map<int>)[]`, `(readonly & [int, string])[]` and a type alias `type RoInts readonly & int[];`. Filling `int[][]` works.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal` on upstream `main` (61fb6bf42fb746f800b851d6ec55d52cb02752c5) with:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    (readonly & int[])[] a = [];
    a[1] = [7];
    io:println(a); // @output [[],[7]]
    any first = a[0];
    io:println(first is readonly); // @output true
}
```

**Actual:**
```
error: no filler value
        at main(readonly-filler-v.bal:5)
```

**Expected:** prints `[[],[7]]` then `true` (the filler is a read-only `[]`).

**Spec reasoning:** §5.9.1 FillMember filler value table: "readonly & T — the filler value for T constructed as read-only — if that belongs to the type". The filler for an array type is `[]`, and a read-only `[]` belongs to `readonly & int[]`. §6.7.1 likewise allows omitting trailing tuple members when "the i-th member can be filled in automatically".

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ 61fb6bf42fb746f800b851d6ec55d52cb02752c5

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go toolchain from go.mod

### Related area
Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Other filler issues with different causes: #1050, #1147, #1521.

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Type/Bug

[Bug]: string template with non-string interpolations is not singleton-typed
candidates.body:
### Description
A string template whose interpolations are all singleton-typed should itself get a singleton type. Nutcracker does this when every interpolation is a string (`"ab" s1 = string `a${"b"}`;` is accepted, and `const` templates work), but not when an interpolation is an int/float/boolean literal outside const context.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal` on upstream `main` (61fb6bf42fb746f800b851d6ec55d52cb02752c5) with:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    "ab" s1 = string `a${"b"}`;
    "a1" s2 = string `a${1}`;
    string:Char c = string `${7}`;
    io:println(s1, s2, c); // @output aba17
}
```

**Actual:**
```
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected "a1", got string
 --> tmpl-singleton1-v.bal:5:15
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected string:Char, got string
 --> tmpl-singleton1-v.bal:6:21
```

**Expected:** compiles and prints `aba17`.

**Spec reasoning:** §6.6.1: "The static type of the result of the string-template-expr is string, modified by the usual singleton typing rules." §6.2.4: "when all subexpressions of the compound expression have a singleton type, then the static type of E is a singleton subtype of T. This subtype is computed by evaluating the expression at compile-time with operands whose values belong to the corresponding singleton types." The literals `1` and `7` have singleton precise types (§6.5), so the templates have types `"a1"` and `"7"` (a `string:Char`).

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ 61fb6bf42fb746f800b851d6ec55d52cb02752c5

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go toolchain from go.mod

### Related area
Type checker

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Related singleton-typing issues: #1262, #1457, #1046.

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Type/Bug

### Suggested assignee(s) (optional)
